evidence.excerpt: A hygrothermal model of a polyphthalamide (PPA) junction box used in crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules was subjected to a global sensitivity analysis using the Sobol variance decomposition method. Nine input parameters were varied: gasket vapour permeability, gasket cross-section width, groove surface roughness, internal air volume, internal polymer sorption isotherm slope, external temperature amplitude, external humidity amplitude, solar irradiance-driven temperature offset, and potting compound surface area. Each parameter was sampled over physically realistic ranges drawn from the literature and from in-house measurements. A total of 18 432 model evaluations were performed. The first-order Sobol index for the time to condensation onset was dominated by gasket vapour permeability (S₁ = 0.41) and external humidity amplitude (S₁ = 0.28). Grove surface roughness had a smaller but non-negligible contribution (S₁ = 0.09). The analysis identifies gasket material selection and installation surface finish as the most impactful design levers for extending the condensation-free service life of PV junction boxes.
